findings.title: Empty Shift range replaces selection with nothing
findings.message: Modifiers are tested with mod.HasFlag(key.Shift) and key.Meta, while the other changed code treats modifiers as bitmasks (1<<key.Shift). If key.Shift is an enum index and not a bit flag, HasFlag is probably correct for bits, but the mixed usage (the `& ^((1<<key.Shift)|(1<<key.Meta))` mask) is fragile. Separately, a Shift range on a range with no valid anchor silently falls back to a single item, and Command-Shift 'Add' replaces nothing, so disabled-only ranges send an empty IDs event that clears selection on plain Shift.
findings.suggestion: Return without calling SelectionChange when ids is empty, and use one consistent modifier test.
findings.evidence: r.node.SelectionChange(ui.ListSelectionEvent{ID: r.node.ID, TargetID: id, IDs: ids, Toggle: mod.HasFlag(key.Meta) && !mod.HasFlag(key.Shift), Add: mod.HasFlag(key.Meta) && mod.HasFlag(key.Shift)})

findings.title: Apply with empty IDs clears selection
findings.message: Apply for a Shift-click range replace returns the range; if the range is empty (all disabled) the selection is cleared. Also Apply's toggle path uses append(result[:i], result[i+1:]...) on a clone, which is fine, but the non-toggle replace path ignores `current` entirely, so a rejected app that calls Apply cannot tell it was a no-op.
findings.suggestion: Guard against empty IDs: if len(ids)==0 return slices.Clone(current).
